h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר א׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Aleph

p: הַתּוֹסָפוֹת
Tosafos
(שַׁבָּת פ"ז: דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְאוֹתוֹ)
(Shabbos 87b, s.v. V'oso)
הֵבִיא טַעַם שֶׁנִּקְרָא שַׁבָּת זֶה שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל
brought a reason why this Shabbos is called Shabbos HaGadol:
לְפִי שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בּוֹ נֵס גָּדוֹל
because a great miracle was performed on it,
כִּדְאָמְרִינַן בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
as we say in the Midrash:
כְּשֶׁלָּקְחוּ הַפְּסָחִים בְּאוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת שֶׁהָיָה עָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ,
when they took the Pesach lambs on that Shabbos, which was the tenth of the month,
נִתְקַבְּצוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת וְכוּלֵּי
the firstborn gathered, etc.,
וְעָשׂוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת מִלְחָמָה וְהָרְגוּ רַבִּים מֵהֶם,
and the firstborn waged war and killed many of them
הֲדָא הוּא דִּכְתִיב:
this is what is written:
לְמַכֵּה מִצְרַיִם בִּבְכוֹרֵיהֶם
"To Him who smote Egypt through their firstborn"
עַד כָּאן.
(up to here).
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין לָמָּה נִקְרָא זֶה נֵס גָּדוֹל?
And one must understand: why is this called a "great miracle"?
הָא כַּמָּה נִסִּים גְּדוֹלִים מִזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה!
Surely many miracles greater than this were performed!
וּמַה גַּם שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַבְּכוֹרוֹת
And what is more, this took place through the firstborn themselves
וְלֹא נַעֲשָׂה כְּלָל בְּצִיוּוּי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ
and was not done at all by the command of Hashem, may He be blessed,
וְלֹא נֶחְשַׁב כְּלָל בֵּין הַמַּכּוֹת.
nor was it counted among the plagues at all.
גַּם מַה תּוֹעֶלֶת הָיָה מִזֶּה לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם?
Also, what benefit did this bring to the Exodus from Egypt?
וּבְעִיקַּר הַלָּשׁוֹן "נֵס גָּדוֹל" קָשֶׁה לְהָבִין:
And regarding the very expression "great miracle," it is difficult to understand:
מַה שַׁיָּיךְ אֵצֶל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נֵס גָּדוֹל?
how does "great miracle" apply to Hashem, may He be blessed?
הֲיִפָּלֵא מֵה' דָּבָר?!
"Is anything too wondrous for Hashem?"
גַּם קוּשְׁיַת הַמְּפָרְשִׁים
Also, there is the question of the commentators:
דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לִקְבּוֹעַ בְּיוֹם י' לַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִקְרָא יוֹם גָּדוֹל,
that it should have been established on the tenth day of the month to be called "Great Day,"
וְלָמָּה קְבָעוּהוּ בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם פֶּסַח?
so why did they establish it on the Shabbos before Pesach?
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת הָא דְּנִקְבַּע בְּיִחוּד בְּמִזְמוֹר הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל:
However, in truth, the reason it was specifically established in the psalm of the Great Hallel:
לְמַכֵּה מִצְרַיִם בִּבְכוֹרֵיהֶם כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ,
"To Him who smote Egypt through their firstborn, for His kindness is forever,"
כְּפִי מִדְרָשָׁם, אַף שֶׁזֶּה לֹא נֶחְשַׁב בְּמִנְיַן הַמַּכּוֹת
according to their Midrashic exposition, even though this was not counted in the number of the plagues,
וְלֹא הוּזְכְּרוּ שָׁם שְׁאָר הַמַּכּוֹת
and the other plagues were not mentioned there
הָעִנְיָן הוּא דִּכְתִיב
the matter is as it is written
(יְשַׁעְיָה מ"ג, ג')
(Yeshayahu 43:3):
נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּךָ וּלְאֻמִּים תַּחַת נַפְשֶׁךָ.
"I have given Egypt as your ransom, etc., and I will give a man in your place, and peoples in place of your soul."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ קִטְרוּג עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
That is, when there is heavenly prosecution against Israel, God forbid,
נוֹתֵן ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כּוֹפֶר תַּחְתָּם מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
Hashem, may He be blessed, gives a ransom in their place from the nations of the world,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְבַּטֵּל הַקִּטְרוּג.
and through this the prosecution is nullified.
וְאָמַר "נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם" לְשׁוֹן עָבָר,
And it says, "I have given Egypt as your ransom," in the past tense,
וְ"אֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּךָ"
and "I will give a man (Adam) in your place,"
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ
which they expounded
(בְּרָכוֹת ס"ב:)
(Berachos 62b):
אַל תִּקְרֵי אָדָם אֶלָּא אֱדוֹם,
"Do not read 'Adam' (man), rather 'Edom'"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכֵּן יִהְיֶה בַּמַּלְכוּת הָרְבִיעִית גַּם כֵּן.
meaning that so it will be in the fourth kingdom as well.
וְהֵיכָן מָצִינוּ שֶׁנִּיתְּנוּ הַמִּצְרִים לְכוֹפֶר?
And where do we find that the Egyptians were given as a ransom?
הוּא מַה שֶּׁהִכּוּ הַבְּכוֹרוֹת בַּאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם.
It is when the firstborn struck down their own fathers.
וְאָמַר עַל זֶה:
And regarding this it says:
מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ בְעֵינַי נִכְבַּדְתָּ וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ
"Since you were precious in My eyes, you were honored, and I have loved you."
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁיִּהְיֶה קִטְרוּג עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ,
That is, even though there was prosecution against Israel asking, "How are these different from those?"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁקִּיטְרֵג הַסָּמֶ"ךְ מֵ"ם וְשַׂר שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם,
as the Satan and the guardian angel of Egypt prosecuted,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
as they said in Midrash Rabbah
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ז')
(Shemos Rabbah 21:7)
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ק"ע:),
אַךְ "וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ", אַהֲבָה בְּלֹא טַעַם,
nevertheless, "I have loved you"—an unconditional love without reason,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
along the lines of what is said
(מַלְאָכִי א', ב')
(Malachi 1:2):
בַּמָּה אֲהַבְתָּנוּ, הֲלוֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב וְגוֹמֵר וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב,
"'Wherein have You loved us?' 'Was not Esav brother to Yaakov?' etc., 'Yet I loved Yaakov.'"
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁעֵשָׂו עוֹשֶׂה כְּמַעֲשֵׂה יַעֲקֹב אוֹ לְהֵיפֶךְ חָלִילָה,
That is, even if Esav acts like Yaakov or vice versa, God forbid,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם "וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב" אַהֲבָה בְּלֹא טַעַם,
nevertheless "I loved Yaakov"—an unconditional love without reason,
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם.
and for this reason "I have given Egypt as your ransom."
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ
And in the Midrash
(תְּהִלִּים קל"ו)
(Tehillim 136)
אִיתָא:
it is stated:
שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא הָרְגוּ הַבְּכוֹרוֹת בַּאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם.
"Six hundred thousand did the firstborn slay among their fathers."
הַמִּסְפָּר סוֹכֵם לְמִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא,
This number equals the number of the Children of Israel, six hundred thousand,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה לְכוֹפֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה קִטְרוּג עֲלֵיהֶם.
because this served as a ransom for Israel so that there would be no prosecution against them.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נַעֲשָׂה נֵס זֶה עַל יְדֵי הַבְּכוֹרוֹת עַצְמָן שֶׁלֹּא בְּצִיוּוּי,
And because of this, this miracle happened through the firstborn themselves without a command,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן הָיָה עַל גּוּף דָּבָר זֶה קִטְרוּג: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ!
for otherwise there would have been prosecution over this very act: "How are these different from those?"
וְנָתַן ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֵב הַבְּכוֹרוֹת שֶׁיַּהַרְגוּ אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם מֵעַצְמָן מִפְּנֵי פַּחַד מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת,
So Hashem, may He be blessed, put it into the hearts of the firstborn to kill their fathers on their own out of fear of the Plague of the Firstborn,
וְאָז נַעֲשׂוּ הֵם כּוֹפֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
and then they became a ransom for Israel.
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד כְּתִיב:
And similarly regarding the future it is written:
וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּךָ
"And I will give a man in your place"
אַל תִּקְרֵי אָדָם אֶלָּא אֱדוֹם,
do not read "Adam," rather "Edom,"
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל קְלִיפּוֹת שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת,
who is the root of all the husks of the seventy nations,
וְהַשַּׂר שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא עַל כָּל שָׂרֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
and whose guardian angel rules over all the guardian angels of the nations of the world.
וּלְאֻמִּים תַּחַת נַפְשֶׁךָ
"And peoples in place of your soul"
לְאֻמִּים הַיְינוּ כָּל הַשִּׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת,
"peoples" refers to all seventy nations,
שֶׁמִּקְּלִיפּוֹת עֵשָׂו מִסְתָּעֵף שִׁבְעִים קְלִיפּוֹת,
for from the husks of Esav branch out seventy husks,
שְׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ מִימִינָא וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ מִשְּׂמָאלָא,
thirty-five on the right and thirty-five on the left,
וְזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשִּׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת.
and this is the root of the seventy nations.
וְכָל אוּמָּה וְאוּמָּה מַכְנִיסִים הָרַע מִקְּלִיפּוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶן גַּם בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And each and every nation injects the evil from their husks into the heart of Israel as well,
וְלָכֵן יִהְיוּ הֵם כּוֹפֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
and therefore they will be a ransom for Israel
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בְּעִנְיַן נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגֵיהִנּוֹם),
(as explained elsewhere regarding one taking his own share and his fellow's share in Gehinnom),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and as it is said
(וַיִּקְרָא ט"ז, כ"ב)
(Vayikra 16:22):
וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם
"And the goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities"
עֲוֹנוֹת תָּם
the iniquities of the "wholesome man" (Yaakov)
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס"ה, ט"ו).
(Bereishis Rabbah 65:15).
וְאָז לֶעָתִיד גַּם כֵּן יְסַבֵּב ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּהַרְגוּ זֶה בָּזֶה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הֵם כּוֹפֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And then in the future as well, Hashem, may He be blessed, will bring about that they slay one another so that they serve as a ransom for Israel,
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
and similarly what is said
(יְשַׁעְיָה מ"ג, ג')
(Yeshayahu 43:3):
כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא תַּחְתֶּךָ
"Kush and Seva in your place"
שֶׁיִּתְגָּרוּ זֶה בָּזֶה.
that they will provoke one another into conflict.
נִמְצָא מַה שֶּׁהָרְגוּ הַבְּכוֹרוֹת מֵעַצְמָן בַּאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא
Thus it emerges that the firstborn slaying six hundred thousand of their fathers on their own
הָיָה עִיקַּר הַסִּיבָּה לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
was the primary cause for the Exodus from Egypt.
וְהָעִנְיָן מְבוֹאָר בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ
And the matter is explained in Zohar Chadash
(Parshas Balak):
מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ
"Since you were precious (yakarta)"
יָקָר מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ וְכוּלֵּי מַהוּ יָקַרְתָּ?
it should have said "yakar," etc.; what is "yakarta"?
מִכְּלָל דְּאִיהוּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ אִתְיַיקַּר וְכוּלֵּי.
It implies that he made himself precious on his own, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת גַּם מִצַּד הָאָדָם,
That is, there must also be an awakening from man's side,
וְאָז מִתְעוֹרֵר מִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה.
and then the attribute of love is aroused.
וְאַף בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה מְעַט הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And even at the Exodus from Egypt there was a slight awakening from Israel's side,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה א', ל"ו)
(Shemos Rabbah 1:36):
שֶׁעָשׂוּ תְּשׁוּבָה הַבֵּינוֹנִים, וְגַם הָרְשָׁעִים הִרְהֲרוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה,
that the average people repented, and even the wicked contemplated repenting,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד בַּחֲבֵירוֹ לֹא יָדַע אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְבַדּוֹ וְכוּלֵּי.
such that not even one knew of his fellow, only the Holy One, blessed is He, alone, etc.
וְאַף שֶׁהָיָה הַהִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה רַק מִצַּד הַלַּחַץ וְהַדֹּחַק,
And although that thought of repentance was only due to the pressure and distress,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִתְעוֹרֵר אָז מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד וְהָאַהֲבָה בְּלֹא טַעַם:
nevertheless, the attribute of kindness and unconditional love was aroused then:
וְאָנֹכִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ,
"And I have loved you,"
וְנַעֲשׂוּ הַמִּצְרִים כָּפְרָם.
and the Egyptians became their ransom.
וּמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד הוּא מִדַּת הַגְּדוּלָּה,
And the attribute of Chessed is the attribute of Gedulah (Greatness),
שֶׁכֵּן מְשַׁבְּחִין: הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא
for thus we praise: "the Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome,"
נֶגֶד מִדַּת חֶסֶד גְּבוּרָה תִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁהָאָבוֹת מֶרְכָּבָה לָהֶם.
corresponding to the attributes of Chessed, Gevurah, and Tiferes, for which the Patriarchs are chariots.
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ
And so it is stated in the Midrash
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נ"ג, י'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 53:10):
וַיַּעַשׂ אַבְרָהָם מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל
"And Avraham made a great feast"
גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים הָיָה שָׁם.
"The Great One of the worlds was there."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה וְהַחֶסֶד,
That is, then through our father Avraham, peace be upon him, who was refined in the attribute of love and kindness,
נִקְרָא ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אָז גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים.
Hashem, may He be blessed, was called "the Great One of the worlds."
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּיוֹם הִגָּמֵל אֶת יִצְחָק.
And this was on the day Yitzchak was weaned.
דְּ"גָּדוֹל" מוֹרֶה אֵצֶל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת וּתְפִיסַת בְּנֵי אָדָם.
For "Great" regarding Hashem, may He be blessed, indicates without measure, beyond human grasp and comprehension.
וְזֶה נִתְבָּרֵר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּשֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק וְנִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה,
And this was clarified in our father Avraham, peace be upon him, when Yitzchak was born and circumcised at eight days,
וְשֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ נַעֲשָׂה נִימּוֹל,
being circumcised without his conscious intent,
אָז נִקְרָא ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשֵׁם גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים,
then Hashem, may He be blessed, was called by the name "Great One of the worlds,"
וְנִקְרָא אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי בְּלִי טַעַם.
and Avraham was called "My beloved" unconditionally.
וְכֵן נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהוּא מִטַּעַם וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ אַהֲבָה בְּלֹא טַעַם, רַק מִצַּד מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד,
And similarly, "I have given Egypt as your ransom" is because of "and I have loved you"—an unconditional love without reason, solely from the attribute of Chessed
וְנִקְרָא מִטַּעַם זֶה "נֵס גָּדוֹל" שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד הַגָּדוֹל.
and for this reason it is called a "great miracle," because it came from the attribute of HaGadol (the Great).

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Shabbos 87b, s.v. V'oso — "…so on the Shabbos before, the tenth of the month, they took their Pesach lambs; therefore it is called Shabbos HaGadol, for a great miracle was done on it, as the Midrash says: when they took their Pesach lambs that Shabbos, the firstborn of the nations gathered… asked their fathers and Pharaoh to send Israel out and were refused; the firstborn made war and killed many of them, as it says, 'Who struck Egypt through their firstborn.'"

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis 11 — “‘I have given Egypt as your ransom’ refers to Egypt: Hashem put it into the heart of Pharaoh and his people to pursue Israel even after they had sent them out, because there was still an accusation against Israel. They drowned in the sea because Hashem made clear that every claim against Israel comes only through the evil found in Egypt, from which the leaven in the dough entered Israel's heart. ‘Kush and Seva in your stead’ alludes to the war of Zerach the Kushite against Asa: Kush is the root of the blemish of the covenant, and they died by plague and became a ransom for Israel.” Connection: Both read Yeshayahu 43:3 as a ransom that cancels the accusation; Bereishis 11 places Egypt's ransom at the sea and finds Kush and Seva in Zerach's war against Asa.

Elazar applied to him: 'I will give a man (adam) in your place' — read not adam but Edom." Rashi: 'his innards' — the rectum.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 21:7 — "When Israel left Egypt, Samael the angel stood to prosecute them. He said before the Holy One: Master of the world, until now these were serving idols, and You split the sea for them? What did the Holy One do? He handed him Iyov, one of Pharaoh's counselors… 'Let him busy himself with Iyov while Israel goes up out of the sea.'"

All are guilty before You… these serve stars and constellations and those serve stars and constellations; these are immoral and those are immoral; these shed blood and those shed blood."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Malbim, Yeshayahu 43:4 — “‘Since you were precious in My eyes, you were honored, and I have loved you’: a thing is precious because of its rarity, like fine gold and pearls; honored because of its intrinsic standing; and loved because it carries grace. He says: You are precious in My eyes because of the root of your soul, which is from a high place, the rock from which your fathers were hewn; you are honored through your excellence in Torah and good deeds; and I have loved you from the side of will. Therefore, ‘I will give a man in your place’: in place of your body I give a single man, but in place of your soul, which is emanated from on high, I give nations and many peoples.” Connection: Both read ‘and I have loved you’ as a love not earned by Israel's deeds; Malbim sets it apart from the preciousness of their root and the honor of their deeds as a love of pure will, and ties the ransom of nations to it.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Metzora and Shabbos HaGadol 5679 — “The Shabbos before Pesach is called Shabbos HaGadol after the great miracle that occurred then. Miracles are called ‘great’ because they come from Chessed, which is called Gedulah. The term Gedulah, which the Sages explained as the attribute of Chessed, is the flow of kindness with no prior awakening from below. Therefore the work of Creation, when there was as yet no one in the world to awaken anything from below, is called Gedulah. So too Avraham, whose attribute was kindness given without any awakening from the receiver, for he went searching for guests, is called ‘the great man.’ And all the miracles done by the prophets that go beyond nature, not because of the great merit of the recipients, are called Gedulah.” Connection: Both explain ‘great’ in Shabbos HaGadol as Chessed and Gedulah, linked to Avraham; Shem MiShmuel defines Gedulah as kindness that flows with no awakening from below, which matches Rav Tzadok's love without reason.

p: וְהִנֵּה שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי פֶּסַח הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת
Now, the seven days of Pesach correspond to the seven lower attributes,
אֵיךְ שֶׁנְּחַשֵּׁב אִם נְחַשֵּׁב שְׁנֵי יְמֵי הַפֶּסַח לְאֶחָד,
however we calculate it, even if we count the two days of Pesach as one;
אַךְ לְכָל הַדֵּעוֹת שִׁבְעָה יְמֵי הַפֶּסַח הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁבְּחֶסֶד,
yet according to all opinions, the seven days of Pesach correspond to the seven sub-attributes within Chessed,
שֶׁעִיקַּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה מִצַּד הַגְּדוּלָּה וְהַחֶסֶד.
for the essence of the Exodus from Egypt came from Gedulah and Chessed.
וְכֵן חַג הַפֶּסַח הוּא כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And likewise the festival of Pesach corresponds to our father Avraham, peace be upon him
בֵּין כְּשֶׁנְּחַשֵּׁב שִׁבְעָה יְמֵי הַמּוֹעֲדִים כְּנֶגֶד שִׁבְעָה רוֹעִים,
whether we count the seven days of the festivals against the seven shepherds,
בֵּין בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹן שְׁלֹשָׁה רְגָלִים נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת,
or in the reckoning of the three pilgrimage festivals against the three Patriarchs,
תָּמִיד פֶּסַח כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
Pesach always corresponds to our father Avraham, peace be upon him.
וְכֵן לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ מִדַּת אַהֲבָה,
And similarly, to our father Avraham, peace be upon him, whose attribute is love,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(יְשַׁעְיָה מ"א, ח')
(Yeshayahu 41:8):
זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי,
"the seed of Avraham, My beloved,"
וְהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד וְהַגְּדוּלָּה,
and who is a chariot for the attribute of Chessed and Gedulah,
נֶאֱמַר לוֹ בַּמַּחֲזֶה גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְאַחַר כָּךְ יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל.
it was told to him in a vision about the Egyptian exile and that afterward "they shall go out with great wealth."
וְשַׁבָּת "בֵּרַכְתּוֹ מִכָּל הַיָּמִים וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים",
And regarding Shabbos, we say: "You blessed it above all days and sanctified it above all seasons,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת נִכְלְלוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים הַבָּאִים בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו.
meaning that in Shabbos is included the holiness of the festivals that come during the weekdays following it.
וְלָכֵן בְּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁאֵירַע אָז בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁאַחֲרָיו הָיָה חַג הַפֶּסַח,
Therefore, on the tenth of the month, which occurred then on the Shabbos after which was the festival of Pesach,
נִתְעוֹרֵר אָז מִדַּת הַגְּדוּלָּה
the attribute of Gedulah was aroused then,
וְנַעֲשָׂה הַנֵּס גָּדוֹל שֶׁהָרְגוּ הַבְּכוֹרוֹת בַּאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא,
and the great miracle occurred that the firstborn slew six hundred thousand of their fathers,
וְנָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם,
and "I have given Egypt as your ransom"
אַף שֶׁהָיוּ מוּקָּפִים מִכָּל צַד מִקְּלִיפּוֹת מִצְרַיִם, רַק מִטַּעַם וַאֲנִי אֲהַבְתִּיךָ.
even though they were surrounded on every side by the husks of Egypt, solely because of "and I have loved you."
וְהִנֵּה כְּתִיב שָׁם:
Now it is written there:
כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא תַּחְתֶּךָ,
"Kush and Seva in your place,"
וְלֹא נִזְכַּר בְּשׁוּם מָקוֹם שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא כּוֹפֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
yet it is not mentioned anywhere that Kush and Seva became a ransom for Israel,
וְגַם לֹא נִזְכַּר שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל;
nor is it mentioned that they enslaved Israel;
וְאִם קָאֵי לֶעָתִיד, לָמָּה נִזְכְּרוּ הֵם בְּיִחוּד וְלֹא שְׁאָר אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַמְּפוּרְסָמִים,
and if it refers to the future, why were they singled out specifically and not the other famous nations of the world,
וְלָמָּה לֹא נִכְלְלוּ בִּכְלַל "וּלְאֻמִּים תַּחַת נַפְשֶׁךָ"?
and why were they not included in the general category of "and peoples in place of your soul"?
אַךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַגָּלוּת הוּא לְתִיקּוּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
However, the root of all exile is to rectify the blemish of the covenant,
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ פְּגַם מֵהַנָּחָשׁ.
which was the root of the blemish from the serpent.
וְכֵן הָיָה גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁנִּקְרָא עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ,
And so was the Egyptian exile, which is called "the nakedness of the land,"
כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּתַקְּנוּ פְּגַם זֶה.
in order that they rectify this blemish.
וְהָיָה זֶה מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדוּרִים מִן הָעֶרְוָה,
And this came from Israel's side, as they fenced themselves off from immorality,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
as they said in the Midrash
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד', כ"ה):
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:25):
שָׂרָה יָרְדָה לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדְרָה עַצְמָהּ מִן הָעֶרְוָה
"Sarah went down to Egypt and fenced herself off from immorality,
וְנִגְרְרוּ כָּל הַנָּשִׁים בִּזְכוּתָהּ;
and all the women followed in her merit;
יוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה
Yosef went down to Egypt and fenced himself off from immorality,
וְנִגְרְרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ.
and all the men followed in his merit."
וְאַף שֶׁהָיָה קְלִיפַּת מִצְרַיִם מַקֶּפֶת אוֹתָם מִכָּל צַד,
And even though the husk of Egypt surrounded them on every side,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(דְּבָרִים ד', ל"ד)
(Devarim 4:34):
גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי
"a nation from the midst of a nation"
אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מְגַדְּלֵי בְּלוֹרִיּוֹת וְכוּלֵּי,
"these and those grew locks of hair, etc."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה
as they said in Vayikra Rabbah
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיוּ גְּדוּרִים מִן הָעֶרְוָה,
nevertheless they fenced themselves off from immorality;
מִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִתְעוֹרֵר "נָתַתִּי כָפְרְךָ מִצְרַיִם".
because of this, "I have given Egypt as your ransom" was aroused.
וְזָכַר אַחַר כָּךְ: כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא תַּחְתֶּךָ.
And afterward it mentions: "Kush and Seva in your place."
דְּכוּשׁ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְלִיפַּת קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית,
For Kush is the root of the husk of the corruption of the covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(סַנְהֶדְרִין ק"ח:)
(Sanhedrin 108b)
שֶׁחָם שִׁימֵּשׁ בַּתֵּיבָה,
that Cham cohabited in the Ark
וְזֶה הָיָה אָז פְּגַם הַבְּרִית שֶׁהוּזְהֲרוּ עַל זֶה אָז
and that was the blemish of the covenant at that time, regarding which they had been warned
וְחָם לָקָה בְּעוֹרוֹ, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
and Cham was smitten in his skin, as it is stated in the Midrash
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ל"ו, ז'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 36:7):
יָצָא חָם מְפוּחָם.
"Cham emerged blackened."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת,
And just as in Israel holiness resides in the firstborn,
כֵּן זֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עִיקַּר הַזּוֹהֲמָא בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת,
so correspondingly among the nations of the world the main filth resides in the firstborn:
וְכוּשׁ בְּכוֹרוֹ שֶׁל חָם, וּסְבָא בְּכוֹרוֹ שֶׁל כּוּשׁ,
and Kush was the firstborn of Cham, and Seva was the firstborn of Kush,
וְהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ זוֹהֲמַת הַקְּלִיפָּה מִזֶּה.
and they are the root of the filth of the husk from this.
וְלָכֵן נִזְכַּר "כּוּשׁ וּסְבָא תַּחְתֶּךָ",
And therefore "Kush and Seva in your place" is mentioned:
שֶׁיִּתֵּן ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבָּם שֶׁיִּתְגָּרוּ זֶה בָּזֶה,
that Hashem, may He be blessed, will put it into their hearts to provoke one another into war,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיוּ כּוֹפֶר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
and through this they will be a ransom for Israel.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר: וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּךָ
And afterward it is said: "And I will give a man in your place"
אַל תִּקְרֵי אָדָם אֶלָּא אֱדוֹם, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל קְלִיפַּת הַשִּׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת;
do not read "Adam," rather "Edom," who is the root of the entire husk of the seventy nations;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ: וּלְאֻמִּים תַּחַת נַפְשֶׁךָ
and afterward: "and peoples in place of your soul"
כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת בִּפְרָט, וְכָאָמוּר.
all the nations in particular, as stated.
וְזֶה שֶׁדָּרַשׁ הַמַּגִּיד:
And this is what the Maggid (reciter of the Haggadah) expounded:
"בְּיָד חֲזָקָה" — זוֹ הַדֶּבֶר;
"'With a strong hand'—this refers to the pestilence";
וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין הַכַּוָּונָה עַל מַכַּת דֶּבֶר שֶׁהָיָה בַּבְּהֵמוֹת,
and certainly the intent is not the plague of pestilence that struck the livestock,
שֶׁבְּמַכָּה זוֹ לֹא יָצְאוּ עוֹד מִמִּצְרַיִם,
for through that plague they did not yet leave Egypt,
וּבִקְרָא כְּתִיב
whereas in the verse it is written
(דְּבָרִים ו', כ"א)
(Devarim 6:21):
וַיּוֹצִיאֵנוּ ה' מִמִּצְרַיִם בְּיָד חֲזָקָה וְגוֹמֵר.
"And Hashem brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand, etc."
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ הַכַּוָּונָה עַל מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת שֶׁעַל יָדָהּ יָצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם,
Perforce, the intent is the Plague of the Firstborn, through which they left Egypt,
וּמַיְיתֵי רְאָיָה מִקְּרָא דְּ"הִנֵּה יַד ה' הוֹיָה בְּמִקְנְךָ",
and it brings proof from the verse "Behold, the hand of Hashem is upon your livestock,"
שֶׁשַּׁיָּיךְ לְשׁוֹן "יַד ה'" עַל מַכַּת דֶּבֶר,
showing that the term "hand of Hashem" applies to a plague of pestilence,
וְכֵן "יָד הַחֲזָקָה" הַיְינוּ מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת.
and similarly "the strong hand" refers to the Plague of the Firstborn.
וְדָרַשׁ: "וּבִזְרֹעַ נְטוּיָה" — זוֹ הַחֶרֶב וְכוּלֵּי;
And it expounded: "'And with an outstretched arm'—this refers to the sword, etc."
וְלֹא מָצִינוּ שׁוּם מַכַּת חֶרֶב בְּמִצְרַיִם!
Yet we do not find any plague of the sword in Egypt!
וְהַכַּוָּונָה עַל חֶרֶב הַבְּכוֹרוֹת בַּאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם,
Rather, the intent is the sword of the firstborn against their fathers,
וְכָאָמוּר שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה הַסִּיבָּה לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
as stated, that this was the cause for the Exodus from Egypt.
דִּבְלֹא זֶה הָיָה הַקִּטְרוּג: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ;
For without this there would have been the prosecution: "How are these different from those?"
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַחֶרֶב שֶׁהָרְגוּ שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא מִמִּצְרַיִם כְּנַפְשׁוֹת מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
Only through the sword with which they slew six hundred thousand Egyptians—matching the number of souls of the Children of Israel
הָיוּ הֵם כּוֹפֶר נֶפֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
did they become a ransom for the soul of Israel.
וְאַחֲרֵי זֶה בְּמַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת נִתְבָּרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁקְּשׁוּרִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ: בְּנִי בְּכוֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And after that, in the Plague of the Firstborn, Israel were clarified as being bound to the root—"My firstborn son, Israel"
יָצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי הַדֶּבֶר שֶׁהוּא מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת, וְכָאָמוּר.
and they went out of Egypt through the pestilence, which is the Plague of the Firstborn, as stated.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 23:2 — "'To take for Himself a nation from the midst of a nation': these were uncircumcised and those were uncircumcised; these grew locks of hair and those grew locks of hair; these wore sha'atnez and those wore sha'atnez. By strict justice Israel would never have been redeemed from Egypt, had the Holy One not bound Himself by oath."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 108b — "The Rabbis taught: Three cohabited in the Ark, and all were punished: the dog, the raven, and Cham. The dog is tied, the raven spits, and Cham was smitten in his skin." Rashi: 'smitten in his skin' — Kush descended from him.
